requirement: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is satisfied.** The implementation covers both obligations, and the tests cover the cases that can occur. I did not run the tests; this is from reading the code and the tests.

**Escaping names and link targets in badge HTML**
- `escape_html` (src/lib.rs:789) escapes `& < > " '`.
- `shield_badge` (src/lib.rs:444) escapes the whole Shields URL before putting it in `src`. It also escapes the label and message in `alt`.
- `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:285) escapes the requirement name used in the `id` attribute. It escapes the detail-page `href` that is used in both the badge link and the "See evidence" link. The explanatory comment says valid names contain no HTML-special characters, so this escaping is defensive.
- `replace_references` (src/lib.rs:384) escapes the reference `href` built from the target chapter path and anchor.
- Other uses of `shield_badge` (the evidence-state badge in src/index.rs `render_detail_sections`) go through the same escaping helper.
- Other `escape_html` callers (src/commands.rs, src/fixme.rs, src/index.rs, src/terms.rs) are outside the badge surface. They only add escaping for other content.

**Encoding badge text in Shields.io path components**
- `shield_path_component` (src/lib.rs:461) percent-encodes every byte except `A-Za-z0-9.`.
- It maps space to `_`, `_` to `__` and `-` to `--`. These are Shields' own escapes for characters that would otherwise change the path structure.
- Anything else, including `/ ? # % & < > " '` and non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes, becomes `%XX`. So punctuation cannot add path segments, query parameters or fragments.
- Both the label and the message go through this function.

**Marking**
- Every function that implements the behaviour carries an `{impl}` marker for this requirement. The inline marker on the `href` escaping in `replace_references` and the one on `escaped_name` in `replace_definitions` cover the call sites.
- I found no unmarked implementation of this requirement. Behaviour such as term anchors and phrase escaping is attributed to other requirements.

**Tests**
- `badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped` (src/lib.rs:1077) feeds `/ ? # % & < > " '` and a non-ASCII character. It asserts the exact encoded URL, including `&` in the query string, and the HTML-escaped `alt` text.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` (src/lib.rs:1133) checks the `_` to `__` and `-` to `--` mapping and the space to `_` mapping.
- `reference_link_targets_are_escaped` (src/lib.rs:1096) is an end-to-end check. It gives the target chapter a path containing `& " < >` and asserts the rendered `href` is escaped and contains no raw `"q"` or `<x>`.
- The only untested part is escaping of the definition-side name and detail `href` inside `replace_definitions`. Valid names cannot contain special characters, and the `href` uses the same helper that the other tests exercise. This is a minor gap.

text: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
